report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/council/bus.py chunk 1 of 3: constants, hashing, identity, path resolution, and secret floor scan helpers.
risks: council_store_path | medium | Suggests filename-safe by validation but _check_council_id only checks a regex; validation is permissive (allows dots, hyphens, underscores) and does not guard against reserved names or path traversal beyond separators; a filename like 'CON' on Windows or '..' (though regex forbids leading dot) could be problematic. | Confirm whether _check_council_id is the only guard and whether Windows reserved names are considered.

_scan_texts | medium | Docstring claims the path tier is never skipped, but _scan_texts only calls secret_floor_rule('', str(t)); the path tier is run separately by _scan_paths, but this helper does not enforce that _scan_paths is always called. If a caller uses _scan_texts without _scan_paths, the path tier is skipped. | Inspect callers of _scan_texts to confirm they always call _scan_paths for evidence paths.

_resolve_store | low | The refusal check only compares against the resolved forbidden dir; if _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR is a symlink or if the council store path is relative and cwd changes, the resolution might differ. | Confirm that _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR.resolve() is stable and that council_store_path is always used with an absolute base.

canonical_body | low | The docstring says 'Uniform across turn and roster records' but the code simply excludes _NON_BODY_FIELDS; if roster records have different position fields, they might be included incorrectly. | Check roster record schema to confirm the same exclusion set is correct.

handoff.purpose: Defines constants, hashing helpers, identity/path resolution, and secret floor scanning helpers for the council transcript.

symbols.name: ENTRY_VERSION
symbols.note: String constant 'dcouncil/1' marking the transcript format version.

symbols.name: ANCHOR_VERSION
symbols.note: String constant 'dcouncil-anchor/1' marking the anchor format version.

symbols.name: ROOT
symbols.note: Path to the repository root, computed as parents[2] of this file.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_COUNCIL_DIR
symbols.note: Default directory for council transcripts: <ROOT>/runs/council.

symbols.name: _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR
symbols.note: Path to the memory ledger directory (<ROOT>/memory) that council writes must never touch.

symbols.name: TURN_STATUS
symbols.note: Tuple of allowed turn statuses: spoke, refused, unavailable, budget_exhausted, anomaly. Deliberately excludes 'ok'.

symbols.name: UNAVAILABLE_REASONS
symbols.note: Fixed vocabulary for machine reasons when a participant is unavailable.

symbols.name: ANOMALY_REASONS
symbols.note: Fixed vocabulary for anomaly reasons.

symbols.name: PARTICIPANT_OUTCOMES
symbols.note: Fixed vocabulary for participant outcomes in the roster.

symbols.name: MAX_CONTENT_CHARS
symbols.note: Fail-closed ceiling on a single turn's content length: 200,000 characters.

symbols.name: _ACTOR_RE
symbols.note: Regex for actor ids: council.<vendor>.<model> per ADR-010.

symbols.name: _COUNCIL_ID_RE
symbols.note: Regex for council ids: alphanumeric, dot, underscore, hyphen, up to 64 chars, no leading dot.

symbols.name: _SHA256_RE
symbols.note: Regex for 64-character lowercase hex SHA-256 digests.

symbols.name: _WRITE_LOCK
symbols.note: Threading lock to serialize chain writes.

symbols.name: _NON_BODY_FIELDS
symbols.note: Frozenset of position/identity fields excluded from body_sha: ts, prev, entry_sha, id, body_sha.

symbols.name: _ALLOWED_TURN_KEYS
symbols.note: Frozenset of accepted caller keys for a turn record. Unknown keys are refused loudly.

symbols.name: _ALLOWED_META_KEYS
symbols.note: Frozenset of accepted keys inside the meta dict.

symbols.name: _ALLOWED_PARTICIPANT_KEYS
symbols.note: Frozenset of accepted keys for participant roster records.

symbols.name: _APPEND_CACHE
symbols.note: Dict cache keyed by resolved path for per-store append index; invalidated by file size and mtime_ns.

symbols.name: canonical_body
symbols.note: Returns a copy of the record excluding _NON_BODY_FIELDS.

symbols.name: canonical_body_json
symbols.note: Returns JSON serialization of canonical_body with sort_keys, compact separators, and ensure_ascii.

symbols.name: _body_sha
symbols.note: Returns SHA-256 hex digest of canonical_body_json(record) encoded UTF-8.

symbols.name: _entry_sha
symbols.note: Returns SHA-256 of (prev or '') + NUL + body_sha + NUL + ts.

symbols.name: _now_iso
symbols.note: Returns current UTC time as ISO format string.

symbols.name: actor_id
symbols.note: Returns 'council.<vendor>.<model>'.

symbols.name: evidence_ref
symbols.note: Returns dict with path (backslashes replaced) and sha256 of the given bytes.

symbols.name: council_store_path
symbols.note: Validates council_id and returns Path(base_dir or DEFAULT_COUNCIL_DIR) / '<council_id>.jsonl'.

symbols.name: anchor_path
symbols.note: Returns the anchor file path by appending '.anchor.json' to the store path's name.

symbols.name: _check_council_id
symbols.note: Raises ValueError if council_id is not a string or does not match _COUNCIL_ID_RE.

symbols.name: _resolve_store
symbols.note: Resolves the store path and refuses any path under the memory directory.

symbols.name: _scan_paths
symbols.note: Scans each path individually via secret_floor_rule(str(p), '') and returns the first hit.

symbols.name: _scan_texts
symbols.note: Scans each non-empty string via secret_floor_rule('', str(t)) and returns the first hit.

symbols.name: _meta_strings
symbols.note: Returns list of string values from meta dict, sorted by key, skipping non-strings and empty strings.

symbols.name: _scan_turn
symbols.note: Starts at line 218 but body is not in this chunk; signature indicates it returns str | None.

claims.text: An APPEND-ONLY, HASH-CHAINED JSONL file per council at runs/council/<council_id>.jsonl.
claims.why: DEFAULT_COUNCIL_DIR is ROOT/runs/council and council_store_path returns <base_dir>/<council_id>.jsonl; append-only and hash-chaining are implemented in later chunks (not visible here) but the path constant and filename pattern match.

claims.text: every line carries the SHA of the line before it, so a flipped byte or a deleted INTERIOR line breaks the chain and verify_chain NAMES the offending 1-indexed line.
claims.why: The hashing helpers (_entry_sha) implement the chaining, but verify_chain is not in this chunk; the claim about naming the line cannot be observed here.

claims.text: TAIL truncation (any prefix of a valid chain is itself a valid chain) is caught only against the head/count ANCHOR persisted beside the transcript and re-checked on every verify.
claims.why: anchor_path exists and the anchor file is separate, but the verification logic is in later chunks; this chunk does not show how truncation is caught.

claims.text: It deliberately REIMPLEMENTS memstore.py's two-SHA discipline instead of importing it, and it must never write to the memory ledger.
claims.why: The chunk defines its own _body_sha and _entry_sha rather than importing memstore; _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR and _resolve_store enforce refusal of memory paths.

claims.text: Any store path under <repo>/memory/ is refused loudly by _resolve_store.
claims.why: _resolve_store resolves the path and raises ValueError if it is relative to _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR.resolve().

claims.text: body_sha -- sha256 over json.dumps(canonical_body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=True) where canonical_body is the record MINUS the four position/identity fields ts, prev, entry_sha, id (and body_sha itself).
claims.why: canonical_body excludes _NON_BODY_FIELDS (which includes ts, prev, entry_sha, id, body_sha); canonical_body_json uses exactly those arguments; _body_sha hashes the UTF-8 bytes of that JSON.

claims.text: entry_sha -- sha256(prev + "\0" + body_sha + "\0" + ts), the chain link. Genesis prev is None and folds in as "".
claims.why: _entry_sha builds payload = (prev or "") + "\0" + body_sha + "\0" + ts and hashes it.

claims.text: Unlike memstore, a turn's id is entry_sha[:16], not body_sha[:16]
claims.why: The id assignment is not in this chunk; _entry_sha exists but the slicing is not shown.

claims.text: there is NO dedupe. A council transcript is a log of EVENTS: two participants may legitimately emit byte-identical bodies, and deduping the second away would erase a voice from the record.
claims.why: No deduplication logic is visible in this chunk; the append logic is in later chunks.

claims.text: append_round takes a whole round's turns in ANY completion order, sorts them by the vendor-namespaced actor id, assigns seq at chain time, and stamps ONE chain timestamp for the round.
claims.why: append_round is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Real per-turn wall-clock lives in meta.latency_ms / meta.started_ts, which are body content, not chain position.
claims.why: The meta fields are allowed by _ALLOWED_META_KEYS, but their usage is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: PATH channel: every evidence path, INDIVIDUALLY.
claims.why: _scan_paths iterates over each path individually and calls secret_floor_rule(str(p), "").

claims.text: CONTENT channel: the turn content, every ref, and every metadata string, each scanned on its own -- never over the assembled turn.
claims.why: _scan_texts and _meta_strings exist, but the full _scan_turn body is not in this chunk; the claim about scanning every ref and metadata string cannot be fully verified here.

claims.text: A hit REFUSES the turn -- no redact-and-send, no redact-and-store. In its place a status="refused" receipt is chained naming ONLY the rule label (a fixed string, never matched text).
claims.why: The refusal logic is in _scan_turn (truncated at line 218) and append functions in later chunks; not visible here.

claims.text: ONE CARVE-OUT, DELIBERATE: withheld (paths an egress lane declined to send) is scanned with the CONTENT channel only, never the path channel.
claims.why: The handling of withheld is not in this chunk; it likely appears in _scan_turn or append functions.

claims.text: EVERY REQUESTED PARTICIPANT PRODUCES EXACTLY ONE CHAINED TURN PER ROUND
claims.why: The round/participant chaining logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A turn is one of these and nothing else. There is deliberately no "ok" here
claims.why: TURN_STATUS is defined as a tuple containing exactly the five listed statuses, and "ok" is absent.

claims.text: Machine reasons -- fixed vocabulary, so "why is this council degraded?" is answerable by a filter and not by reading prose.
claims.why: UNAVAILABLE_REASONS is a tuple of fixed strings; ANOMALY_REASONS also fixed.

claims.text: Fail-closed ceiling on a single turn. Transcript tokens grow as O(V^2 R^2), not O(V R); the per-council budget lives in session.py, but no single turn may blow the file up on its own.
claims.why: MAX_CONTENT_CHARS is defined, but its enforcement is not in this chunk; the growth claim is not testable here.

claims.text: ADR-010 actor-namespace rule, pinned to the MODEL and not just the vendor
claims.why: _ACTOR_RE requires council.<vendor>.<model> with vendor lowercase and model with letters/digits/dots/colons/plus/hyphen; actor_id builds exactly that.

claims.text: A key outside this set is REFUSED loudly, never dropped: a silently dropped field lets two semantically distinct turns canonicalise to the same body and hands the caller a success id for a turn never recorded.
claims.why: The key validation is not in this chunk; only the allowed set is defined.

claims.text: Per-store append index: tail entry_sha + record/turn counts, keyed by resolved path and invalidated by the file's (size, mtime_ns).
claims.why: _APPEND_CACHE is defined but its population and invalidation logic are not in this chunk.

claims.text: The content projection body_sha is taken over: everything EXCEPT the position/identity fields. Uniform across turn and roster records so the chain walk needs no per-record-type branch.
claims.why: canonical_body excludes all fields in _NON_BODY_FIELDS regardless of record type; the exclusion set is constant.

claims.text: The exact bytes hashed. Exposed so a test can assert determinism against the canonical form rather than against a digest it cannot inspect.
claims.why: canonical_body_json returns the JSON string with deterministic serialization (sort_keys, fixed separators, ensure_ascii).

claims.text: council.<vendor>.<model> per ADR-010. An unknown model id is recorded as the literal unknown by the CALLER -- never omitted, never inferred.
claims.why: actor_id simply formats the string; the caller's handling of unknown models is not in this chunk.

claims.text: One evidence citation: the path as given plus the sha256 of the exact bytes shown to the model. Two participants citing "the file" may have been shown different bytes; without this the transcript records a citation that cannot be reproduced.
claims.why: evidence_ref returns a dict with the path (backslashes normalized) and the SHA-256 of the provided bytes.

claims.text: <base_dir>/<council_id>.jsonl. council_id is filename-safe by validation, not by sanitising: a silently rewritten id would point two councils at one transcript.
claims.why: The path construction is correct, but the claim about filename-safety relies on _check_council_id's regex, which is permissive (allows dots, underscores, hyphens) and does not guard against reserved names or path traversal beyond separators; the validation does not sanitise, but it also does not guarantee absolute safety on all platforms. The claim is partially checkable; the regex permits characters that could be problematic on some filesystems, but the code does not sanitise. I'll mark it UNCHECKABLE because the full set of filename constraints is not specified.

claims.text: The head/count anchor beside the transcript. Separate file on purpose: the chain walk cannot detect tail truncation from a truncated file alone.
claims.why: anchor_path returns a separate file with .anchor.json appended; the reasoning is plausible and the separation is implemented.

claims.text: Resolve and REFUSE any path under <repo>/memory/. Council turns must never reach the memory ledger (see module docstring).
claims.why: _resolve_store resolves the path and raises ValueError if it is inside _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR.

claims.text: PATH channel, one path at a time -- so a hit is attributable to one path and a diff that ADDS .env cannot hide inside a blob.
claims.why: _scan_paths iterates over each path individually and calls secret_floor_rule with that path alone.

claims.text: CONTENT channel, one string at a time. path="" here is correct and is NOT the forbidden whole-prompt call: the path tier is run separately over every evidence path above, so it is never skipped.
claims.why: _scan_texts does scan each string individually with path="", but the claim that the path tier is never skipped depends on callers always invoking _scan_paths; this chunk does not show the call sites. The helper itself does not enforce that.

observations.what: council_store_path docstring claims filename-safe by validation, but _check_council_id allows dots, underscores, hyphens and does not guard against reserved names (e.g., 'CON' on Windows) or other filesystem quirks; the regex is broad.
_scan_texts docstring asserts the path tier is never skipped, but the helper itself does not call _scan_paths; correctness depends on external callers.

canonical_body docstring claims uniformity across turn and roster records, but the exclusion set is fixed; if roster records use different field names for identity, the projection would differ. The chunk does not show roster record schema.

_resolve_store only checks against the resolved forbidden dir; if _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR is a symlink or the path resolution changes, the check might be bypassed. The code resolves both sides, so it is likely correct, but symlink races are not handled.
